thread.title: COLUMN: Murder in the morning

author: Locked, Loaded & Half-Cocked Doug Blough
title: COLUMN: Murder in the morning
text:
Let’s all wake up and return to my recent column about sleep. If you alertly recall, I bemoaned the fact my mental depth has been, shall we say, less than peak, so the one thing I nightly look forward to is going to bed sometime around 1 a.m, doing my Wordle, rubbing Kiki’s tummy and then sleeping unabated till noon or shortly thereafter. I ain’t askin’ for much.
But any day now that magical luxury – those indescribably beautiful sounds of silence – will be taken away from us in a cruel twist of fate and timing. Right next door to my townhouse, where Cory and Crystal Kunis and kids lived quietly for the last eight years, will come the sickening, agonizing sounds of so-called progress. The owner of this adjoining residence gave the Kunis family two months to vacate so that he may completely refurbish and sell. Those two months have passed.
A roofer for 50 years, I’m aware of the sounds of construction and the ungodly hours it takes place. About the time I return from my 7 a.m tinkle and Kiki paws me goodnight for the second time, table saws will be grinding, nail guns pounding, drills pulsating and grouchy carpenters screaming, “Get that **!!! sheetrock up here!” It’s the sudden death of a beautiful dream!
What am I supposed to do that time of morning normally spent snoring, stretching and smiling smugly? I got nothin’ to do during those oddball hours between 7 and 5. There’s nothing on TV I’m familiar with. Sure the Price is Right prize girls are stimulating, but that’s temporary. I have nothing to do outside. I don’t have yard work to enjoy; I got rocks, not grass and shrubbery. I love sleeping all morning and worked enough long, hard hours in my life to deserve that at my age, dammit!
“That construction next door won’t last forever,” you say. “It’s just one little townhouse and soon you’ll be sleeping away your mornings like you’ve grown to love with no one to bother you,” ya say. Well, wrong again, Sawdust Breath! Sprague Roofing is on the schedule to soon start re-roofing all five buildings. My brother Jess and I originally shingled all these buildings in 1983, so I know what’s coming. And that was without removing existing shingles, which only multiplies the time and noise. Nail guns and screaming roofers will surround me as far into the future as I can see. Distraught is too impotent a word for what I’m up against and how life is about to change.
It’s not just MY disrupted life I mourn, but my aging dog, Naomi, is at perfect peace with our laid-back, dysfunctional lifestyle. She sleeps cozily next to the bedroom sliding door and waits about half hour after Kiki and I come down before she makes her downward trek and within the hour she’s ready for her early-afternoon poop walk around the block. Then we all settle in for a long night of sports betting on TV until it’s time to start it all over again come 1 a.m.
But alas, all good naps must end. Waking up can be hell … LITERALLY!

But any day now that magical luxury – those indescribably beautiful sounds of silence – will be taken away from us in a cruel twist of fate and timing.
